blocks.text: 1. Feed-Forward Networks
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446020360-301899422.png

Residual Connections, the previous topic, covered the skip connections wrapping every Transformer sublayer. Feed-Forward Networks revisit this technique specifically in the Transformer context, explored throughout this topic.
This is the genuinely second sublayer within every single encoder and decoder layer, a genuinely essential companion to Self-Attention covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Two-Part Layer Structure

This connects back to the encoder layer structure, already covered in The Encoder. Each encoder layer genuinely combines Self-Attention with a feed-forward network, already covered there in general terms.
This topic genuinely explores exactly what that feed-forward network actually does, giving that earlier general description its own complete, dedicated treatment.
3. What This Sublayer Actually Does
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446020361-950639230.png
This connects back to fully connected layers, already covered in Network Architecture. Each position genuinely passes independently through the exact same small, two-layer fully connected network.
This gets applied identically at every single position within the sequence, a genuinely direct reuse of the fully connected layer concept already covered throughout earlier modules in this course.

blocks.text: 4. Position-Wise Independence
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446020361-844724941.png

A genuinely important, distinctive property connects back to Self-Attention, already covered in its own topic. Unlike Self-Attention, already covered there, the feed-forward network genuinely processes each position entirely independently.

This is a genuinely important structural contrast, since Self-Attention genuinely mixes information across positions while the feed-forward network, already covered in this topic, deliberately does not.
5. Expand, Then Compress
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446020361-692873907.png
This connects back to Network Architecture's own capacity concept, already covered in its own topic. The genuinely first linear layer typically expands to a genuinely larger, intermediate dimension.

The genuinely second linear layer then compresses back down to the original dimension, a genuinely deliberate expand-then-compress pattern giving the network genuinely more capacity to process each position's own representation.
6. The Activation Function Used
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446020361-452331913.png
This connects back to ReLU and GELU, both already covered in the Activation Functions module. A genuinely non-linear activation function, commonly ReLU or GELU, sits between these two linear layers.
This directly reuses an activation function already covered there, applied here within the Transformer's own structure, giving this sublayer its own genuinely necessary non-linearity.

blocks.content: The choice between ReLU and GELU, both already covered in this topic, is itself a genuinely real, tunable architectural decision, with GELU becoming increasingly common in more modern Transformer variants.

blocks.text: 7. Shared Weights Across Positions
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446020362-721777615.png
This connects back to parameter sharing, already covered in the Convolution Operation. The exact same feed-forward weights genuinely get reused at every single position within a layer.
This is a genuinely direct parallel to parameter sharing already covered in that earlier topic, just applied here across sequence positions rather than across spatial position within an image.
8. Different Weights Per Layer

A genuinely important, real distinction connects back to stacking multiple encoder layers, already covered in The Encoder. Each genuinely different Transformer layer genuinely has its own separate feed-forward network weights.

This is a genuinely important clarification worth stating explicitly: weights genuinely get shared across positions within a layer, already covered in the previous section, but genuinely not shared across different layers.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing Why The Feed-Forward Network Is Genuinely Necessary Alongside Attention

blocks.alt: Recognizing Why The Feed-Forward Network Is Genuinely Necessary Alongside Attention
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446020362-441627827.png

This connects back to Attention's own genuinely linear, weighted-averaging nature, already covered throughout the Attention Mechanism module. The feed-forward network's own non-linearity, already covered in this topic, adds genuinely necessary representational power.
Every single Transformer layer, already covered throughout this module, is another genuine case where the feed-forward network, already covered, is genuinely a standard, required component.
10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates the feed-forward network's own expand-then-compress computation, applied independently to each position in a sequence, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
sequence_length = 4
hidden_size = 8
intermediate_size = 32  # already covered as expand, then compress in this topic

def relu(x):
    return np.maximum(0, x)

# already covered as shared weights across positions in this topic
W1 = rng.normal(size=(intermediate_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1
W2 = rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, intermediate_size)) * 0.1

def feed_forward(x, W1, W2):
    expanded = relu(x @ W1.T)  # already covered as expand, then compress in this topic
    compressed = expanded @ W2.T
    return compressed

sequence = rng.normal(size=(sequence_length, hidden_size))
output = feed_forward(sequence, W1, W2)  # already covered as position-wise independence in this topic

print(f"Input shape: {sequence.shape}")
print(f"Output shape (unchanged, already covered as expand, then compress in this topic): {output.shape}")
print("\nThe exact same W1 and W2 weights, already covered in this topic, were reused at every single position")

blocks.content: Running this example shows the same feed-forward weights applied independently to every position, expanding then compressing each one's own representation, exactly the mechanism already covered throughout this topic.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: The Feed-Forward Network is the second sublayer within every encoder and decoder layer.
Each position passes independently through the same small, two-layer fully connected network.
Unlike Self-Attention, it processes each position entirely independently, without mixing across positions.
It expands to a larger intermediate dimension, then compresses back down to the original size.
A non-linear activation, commonly ReLU or GELU, sits between the two linear layers.
The same feed-forward weights are shared across every position within one layer.
Different Transformer layers each have their own separate feed-forward network weights.
Its non-linearity adds representational power that Attention alone, being largely linear, lacks.
Next up: Causal Masking, a mechanism ensuring the decoder cannot look ahead at future positions.
